name: LinkedIn
headline: Sign-in and member posting take an afternoon with no review. Company Page posting, analytics and ads need partner approval.

firstTest.text: About 30-60 minutes to a working sign-in and member post, once a Company Page exists and verifies your app.

production.text: Members can sign in and post after ticking two products. Page posting, analytics and ads need Development approval, then Standard tier with a screen recording.

approvalWait.text: None for Sign In with LinkedIn and Share on LinkedIn. The Community Management API form is reviewed by hand, with no published wait time.

whoCanRegister.text: Any member can create an app, but it must link to a Company Page whose admin verifies it. Partner access also needs a registered company.

testMode.text: Any member who consents works. Tokens last 60 days with no refresh token, so users reconnect about every two months.

actions.label: Sign the user in and read their name, photo and email
actions.review: None. Tick 'Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' on the Products tab.

actions.label: Publish a post (text, link, image or video) to the user's own feed
actions.review: None. Tick 'Share on LinkedIn' on the Products tab.

actions.label: Post, comment and react as a Company Page the user administers
actions.review: Community Management API: a Development tier request, then Standard tier with a screen recording. Legal organizations and commercial use only.

actions.label: Read Company Page followers, posts, comments and analytics
actions.review: Same Community Management API review as posting as a Page.

actions.label: Read the user's own posts and comments
actions.review: Closed. LinkedIn is not accepting access requests.

actions.label: Manage or report on a user's ad accounts
actions.review: Advertising API product. Needs approval, then a Standard tier upgrade with a demo video.

steps.title: Get a Company Page ready
steps.detail: Create one at linkedin.com if you have none; its creator is the administrator. A placeholder Page for your product is fine for the self-serve path.

steps.title: Create the developer app
steps.detail: Go to linkedin.com/developers/apps/new. Enter an app name, pick the Company Page, add a logo and accept the terms. Don't use 'LinkedIn' or 'In' in the app name or logo.

steps.title: Get your app verified
steps.detail: On the App Settings tab, click Verify, generate the verification URL and send it to a Page admin (a super admin for Community Management). The app won't work until it's verified.
steps.time: 5 min if you are the admin

steps.title: Add two self-serve products
steps.detail: On the Products tab, request 'Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' and 'Share on LinkedIn'. Both are open to all developers; the Auth tab then lists the matching permissions.

steps.title: Add the redirect address
steps.detail: On the Auth tab, add each callback URL: absolute HTTPS, no # fragment, matching what you send exactly. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into your server secrets.

steps.title: Build the sign-in flow
steps.detail: Send users to LinkedIn's authorization page with the member permissions you need and a random state value. Check the state on return, then swap the code for a token within 30 minutes.

steps.title: Store tokens and plan reconnects
steps.detail: Save the token and its 60-day expiry. Self-serve apps get no refresh token, so prompt users to reconnect before it expires. Asking for a different scope later invalidates earlier tokens.

steps.title: Publish a member post
steps.detail: Ask LinkedIn for the member's id, then create the post with the 2.0.0 protocol version header set. A 201 reply returns the post id.

steps.title: Apply for Community Management access
steps.detail: For Page posting or analytics only: create a NEW app linked to the same verified Page, with no other products. On its Products tab, request Development tier with your legal name, address, website, privacy policy and business email.
steps.time: 1 hr to apply, then review wait

steps.title: Upgrade to Standard tier
steps.detail: After building the integration, submit the Standard tier form with test credentials and a narrated screen recording. Show the full sign-in flow, posting, and how member data appears.
steps.time: half a day to record and submit, then review wait

blockers.title: No Company Page, or nobody to verify the app
blockers.fix: Create a Page first. The app stays unusable until a Page admin approves the verification link; Community Management needs a Page super admin.

blockers.title: Posting as a Page or reading analytics needs partner access
blockers.fix: It's limited to registered legal organizations with commercial use, a verified business email (personal emails fail) and a verified website. Plan for a review, and decide early whether it's worth it.

blockers.title: The Community Management request is greyed out or rejected
blockers.fix: Only request it from a new app that holds no other products. A rejected app can't reapply, so create another app and submit a fresh Development tier request.

blockers.title: Users get logged out every two months
blockers.fix: Access tokens last 60 days. Only approved Marketing Developer Platform partners get 365-day refresh tokens, so for open products show a reconnect prompt before expiry.

blockers.title: Daily posting cap per user
blockers.fix: Share on LinkedIn allows 150 requests per member and 100,000 per app each day (UTC). Community Management Development tier allows 500 requests per app and 100 per member by default. Queue and spread your posts, and don't retry in a loop.

blockers.title: Your agent can't read the user's feed or post history
blockers.fix: Open products don't allow it, and LinkedIn isn't accepting requests for that permission. Design your agent around write-only member posting.

agentCan: Write the sign-in redirect, the state check and the code swap
Store tokens with expiry dates and schedule reconnect prompts before day 60
Fetch the member's id and publish text, link and image posts
Handle 401, 403 and 429 errors and queue posts under the daily cap
Draft the Community Management form answers and the screencast script
youDo: Create or choose the Company Page
Create the developer app, click Verify, and get a Page admin to approve it
Tick the two products on the Products tab and accept the API terms
Verify your business email and submit the Community Management forms, if you need them
Record the Standard tier screencast showing the live sign-in flow
Sign in to LinkedIn as a test member to give consent

drafts.title: Use case for the Community Management Development tier form
drafts.body: [Product name] is a [company type] tool that lets marketing teams manage their LinkedIn Company Page from one place. Page admins connect their Page through the standard LinkedIn OAuth consent screen. Our AI assistant then drafts posts for the admin to approve, publishes approved posts to the Page, and shows post performance and comments back to the admin. We only access Pages where the signed-in member holds an admin role, we do not resell or combine LinkedIn data, and members can disconnect at any time from Settings. Legal entity: [name], [registered address], [website], privacy policy: [URL].

drafts.title: Standard tier screencast script
drafts.body: 1. Show the app login and click Connect LinkedIn. 2. Complete the real consent screen and show the Page being listed. 3. Write a post in the app and publish it to the Page. 4. Open LinkedIn and show the post live. 5. Add a comment as another member and show how it appears in the app, naming the profile fields we display. 6. Show the analytics screen. 7. Show Disconnect and what data is deleted. Narrate each step. Close all other windows first.

drafts.title: Explainer to show users before LinkedIn's consent screen
drafts.body: [Product name] will ask LinkedIn for permission to see your name and email and to publish posts on your behalf. We only post when you approve a draft. LinkedIn will ask you to reconnect about every 60 days. You can remove access any time in LinkedIn under Settings, Data privacy, Permitted services.
